environment: Microsoft Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200; Python 3.13.15; Docker Desktop 4.61.0; sandbox.image python:3.12-slim; tools.test `python -m pytest -v --cov=ledgerlock --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=85`; tools.lint `ruff check . --exclude .claude --exclude .aisef --exclude .opencode`
reproduction: `docker run --rm python:3.12-slim python -m pytest --version` → `No module named pytest`; `docker run --rm python:3.12-slim ruff --version` → executable not found. The preset that wrote this configuration: aisef/cli/harness.py STACK_PRESETS['python'] (`tools.test` = `<py> -m pytest -v`, `tools.lint` = `ruff check .`, `sandbox.image` = `python:3.12-slim`). Every tool call is a fresh `docker run --rm` (aisef/harness/sandbox.py:207), so nothing installed inside a call survives to the next.
`aisef doctor` on such a project reports `sandbox image python:3.12-slim (matches stack)` (aisef/cli/doctor.py:159-162 only flags `alpine:latest`).
gate_or_evidence: aisef/cli/harness.py STACK_PRESETS; aisef/cli/doctor.py sandbox-image check; run.log tool=test/tool=lint lines 60-195
observed: 16 × `tool=test output: /usr/local/bin/python: No module named pytest` (first 14:13:42); `tool=lint FAIL exit=127 … unrunnable=tool not installed or cannot load (not found)` at 14:22:55 and again at 14:54:58 (`exec: "ruff": executable file not found in $PATH`). The first `tool=test PASS` is at 14:40:06 and the first `tool=lint PASS` at 14:55:21: the image acquired pytest and then ruff during the run (see F-9). Until then the three parallel stories could not verify anything.
expected: docs/USAGE-GUIDE.md §init: `init` writes `tools.test`, `tools.lint`, `sandbox.image`, `sandbox.allow_hosts` for the detected stack, and `aisef doctor` says whether the sandbox image matches the stack. docs/SOLUTION.md `sandbox.image`: 'plain alpine has no tools; tests are red for missing tools, not wrong code' — the same failure mode is shipped by the python preset itself, and doctor calls it a match.
severity_note: With the shipped defaults a Python project cannot pass verification inside the sandbox at all; the operator had to supply a toolchain by hand (an author-level intervention) — 'cannot complete the lifecycle without author assistance'. The owner may rule that the preset is meant as a placeholder for a project-built image; then the defect is the doctor's `matches stack` plus the undocumented requirement, still a product path.
